title: Gate: a root below the repo top reads its policy and baseline from the wrong path at the base, so a PR can loosen its own gate
description:
Follow-up from the Stage 1 verdict on opum-ai/test-skills#56 (TS-35 MINOR 1), recorded verbatim on the completed TS-35 record. opum-doc rules a reachable fail-open in a gate is not minor (relayed by the leader).

THE DEFECT. In skills/test-audit/scripts/tmx/gate.py, paths built relative to --root are passed to git show REF:PATH, which resolves from the repo TOP, not from root. When root is a subdirectory of the repo the lookup misses. Sites (current numbering on dev 856292f): the triage read near line 556 (rel_t), the protected_file read near 627 (pf), and _from_base in main() near 658 for the policy file and, when the policy is found, the baseline (rel). TS-35 fixed only _load_list_at (ref:./path).

MEASURED, 2026-10-21, by the opum-marketplace worker with a throwaway script in its scratchpad, not committed. Two repos with identical content, base policy rigor R3, head quarantines a 60-day-old test AND loosens the policy to R1. Control, gate root at the repo top: exit 1, FAIL Art. XI quarantine_days, policy_source base. Gate root = pkg/ below the top, every file under pkg/: exit 0, the line "gate: test-policy.toml does not exist at main; judging by the working-tree policy (first adoption)" then only a WARN under the PR own R1 policy. So the PR chooses its own rules, which the base-policy design exists to prevent. That is reachable in an ordinary layout (a gate root below the repo top, the standard policy file), at any rigor, not only R4+.

NOT MEASURED, inferred only: the triage (~556) and protected_file (~627) sites. A miss there reads as empty, which over-counts self_added and under-protects, both stricter, so they fail closed unless a file of the same relative name exists at the repo top (the reviewer wrong-file arm, which can under-count self_added at R4+). Needs its own measurement.

FIX SHAPE (not built; opum-doc reviews the fix and the leader gives timing): resolve every base lookup the same way, for example REF:./PATH, or a single helper that all four sites use, plus a test per site with a sub-root fixture. Fold the proofs into existing cases under the 95 cap or ask for a measured slot.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A sub-root repo whose PR loosens its own policy is judged by the BASE policy, not the working-tree one (the measured fail-open is closed and a test proves it both ways).
The triage and protected_file base reads resolve the same way as the state files, with a test each, or their harmlessness is measured and recorded.
No collected test case is added beyond the 95 baseline, or each added case carries a leader-approved slot request.

implementationNotes: MEASURED on dev 856292f/2c93d51 with a throwaway script (scratchpad, not committed), gate root pkg/ below the repo top, R4, matrix with one survivor and one duplicate new test. Rule names reported, correct behaviour in brackets. Triage, file present at the base under pkg/ [no triage_needs_approval]: reported triage_needs_approval, a false finding (stricter). Triage, same-named file only at the repo top, change adds its own pkg/ copy [triage_needs_approval]: NOT reported, so a change could triage its own survivor without an approver (fail-open, R4+). protected_file, present under pkg/ at the base [no require_unique_kill]: reported (stricter). protected_file, same-named file only at the repo top, change adds its own pkg/ copy [require_unique_kill]: NOT reported, so a change could protect its own test (fail-open). After the fix all four arms behave as bracketed. Both fail-opens need a same-named file at the repo top, a monorepo layout, so they are narrower than the policy read, which needed nothing at the top.

REVIEW RECORD, 2026-10-21. opum-ai/test-skills#59 APPROVED at eb0fe3c612c4f010311b32dd2050bfacfd4de1f5 by opum-doc (Opus, by ref, on ODOC-496), relayed by the leader; this is the relay, not a verbatim verdict. Per the relay: tests/test_gate.py 25/25 at head, and reverting each of the three sites alone fails exactly test_a_change_cannot_loosen_its_own_gate. Landed as 28bc34bcd9a573a2c98e556a8de01a8e9ec23353. One MINOR, filed as a follow-up bug before the test-skills release (see the follow-up task referencing TS-38): _from_base returns None on any git failure.
finalSummary: Fixed: every base read in gate.py now resolves from the gate root. _from_base (the policy and, once found, the baseline) uses base:./rel; the triage read and the protected_file read go through _from_base instead of a bare git show, so a root below the repo top no longer reads the wrong file or none. Proof, in one existing case and no new collected case (-m "not slow" passes 95, local Python 3.12; repo own gate run locally PASS; CI covers 3.9): test_a_change_cannot_loosen_its_own_gate gains a sub-root CLI arm (loosened policy must exit 1 with policy_source base; it exits 0 on the old code) and four arms for the triage and protected_file reads (unchanged entry, and a same-named file only at the repo top). Mutation, run after the arms were moved there: reverting each of the three sites alone turns that test red. The wrong-file arms sit after the unchanged-file arms, so a mutant dies at the first failing assertion; they were separately proven fail-open on the measurement script. The triage and protected_file sites were measured, not inferred: both are reachable fail-opens when a same-named file exists at the repo top; with none the miss only over-reports. Detail in the implementation note. CI run cited at the PR head.
